## Summary

The three core artifacts are internally consistent and fully coverage-mapped: every functional
requirement (FR-001…FR-013) and every success criterion (SC-001…SC-006) has at least one task, every
task references a file or path that actually exists in the repo, and the plan's Constitution Check is
PASS with the one intentional duplication (`dagster-pipes` pin) surfaced in Complexity Tracking. The
repo's current state matches the "before" picture the plan/research assume (three harness Dockerfiles
each `FROM node:20-slim` with a duplicated `apt-get`/`pip` block; `agent-python` on `python:3.12-slim`;
`scripts/bootstrap.sh` builds no images; README step 4 passes the per-image directory as the build
context — the pre-existing doc bug the plan calls out).

**No CRITICAL or HIGH findings.** One MEDIUM (a stale "smaller" framing left in the `tasks.md` Phase 5
heading that the remediation removed everywhere else) and four LOW findings (a build-time `/workspace`
ownership shift not noted anywhere, a hermetic-only parity approximation, a grep-pattern mismatch, and
a couple of underspecified-but-resolved-downstream items). All are safe to fix as light touch-ups; none
blocks `/speckit-implement`.

## Findings

| ID | Category | Severity | Location(s) | Summary | Recommendation |
|----|----------|----------|-------------|---------|----------------|
| C1 | Inconsistency (terminology) | MEDIUM | tasks.md:174 vs spec.md:107, spec.md:264, plan.md:110 | Phase 5 heading still reads "User Story 3 - **Smaller**, faster harness image builds", contradicting the remediated re-scope: spec US3 was retitled "Common work built and stored once, faster rebuilds" and FR-011/SC-005 explicitly do **not** assert a smaller total. The Phase 5 Goal/Independent Test/Checkpoint bodies were updated to "stored once" but the heading was missed. | Retitle the Phase 5 heading to match spec US3 (e.g. "Common work built and stored once, faster rebuilds") so no artifact still claims a size reduction. |
| U1 | Underspecification (parity) | LOW | data-model.md:23 (base "Final user … root"), tasks.md:74-75; cf. images/agent-claude/Dockerfile:12-13 | Build-time owner of `/workspace` shifts: today each harness runs `USER node` *then* `WORKDIR /workspace`, so the dir is created uid-1000-owned; the base sets `WORKDIR /workspace` while still root, so it is created root-owned. No artifact notes the shift. **Mitigated**: `/workspace` is bind-mounted `rw` at run time for workspace harnesses (`orchestrator/factory.py:800`), so host ownership overrides the image-time owner — hence LOW, not a parity break. | Add one line to data-model.md / research.md noting the image-time `/workspace` owner changes to root and that the runtime bind mount overrides it, so the shift is a conscious no-op rather than an unexamined one. |
| G1 | Coverage gap (parity evidence) | LOW | tasks.md:135-137 (T012), spec.md:64 (US1 Independent Test) | US1's stated Independent Test is "run one existing agent of each harness end to end and confirm report/output match a pre-refactor run"; no task runs an agent end-to-end. Parity is approximated hermetically by `images/tests` (T012). This is **explicitly acknowledged** in T012 and consistent with the FR-008/SC-002 re-definition (functional/format equivalence via unchanged code + unchanged tests). | Accept as-is (documented approximation), or add an optional manual "run one agent per harness end-to-end" verification note referencing quickstart, so the gap between US1's wording and the hermetic check is explicit. |
| I1 | Inconsistency (verification detail) | LOW | tasks.md:163-164 (T015) vs quickstart.md:44 (§4) | T015's literal grep pattern is `apt-get\|^WORKDIR\|python3-pip\|dagster-pipes`, but its own prose and quickstart §4's pattern also include `useradd\|adduser` to guard against user *creation* regressing back in. The two guards should match. | Align T015's regex with quickstart §4 by adding `useradd\|adduser` (harmless today — no harness has such a line — but it makes the two checks identical). |
| A1 | Ambiguity (resolved downstream) | LOW | spec.md:181 (FR-002), spec.md:284 (Assumptions) | FR-002 says "the standard build essentials" without naming the package; it is only pinned to the `build-essential` apt package in Assumptions/research/plan (and flagged open by checklist CHK009). The requirement text itself remains a soft phrase. | Optionally tighten FR-002 to name `build-essential` inline (or leave it — it is unambiguously resolved in Assumptions, plan Primary Dependencies, and tasks T003). |

## Constitution Alignment Issues

None outstanding. The one Principle I trade-off (uniform `build-essential`/`gh` install into every
shell-based agent vs. strict per-agent minimum) was raised as analysis finding **C1** in the prior
cycle and is now surfaced and accepted in spec §Clarifications (2026-09-16 remediation) and plan
Constitution Check §I as a MEDIUM surfaced trade-off — no isolation boundary, network reach,
credential, or mount is widened, so it is not a Principle I violation. Principle VI (Docs Track
Reality) is *improved* by this feature: it corrects the pre-existing README build-context bug
(per-image context vs. the required `images/` context) as part of FR-012. No CRITICAL constitution
conflict exists.

## Unmapped Tasks

None. T001/T002 are Setup, T019/T020 are Polish/cross-cutting (scope + full-quickstart checks); both
roles are legitimate and carry no user story by design.

## Duplication Note (intentional, not a defect)

The `dagster-pipes==1.13.21` pin appears in both `images/agent-base/Dockerfile` (new) and
`images/agent-python/Dockerfile` (standalone). This is the single intentional duplication, forced by
FR-010 keeping `agent-python` off the Node-bearing base, and is documented in plan §Complexity
Tracking with the rejected simpler alternative. Not counted as a duplication defect.
